guide.h2: Why damp is common in Leeds homes
p: Much of Leeds' older housing is solid wall stone and brick: Victorian terraces, back to backs in areas such as Harehills, Beeston and Armley, and inter war semis. These houses were built to breathe. Damp problems often start when that balance is upset, by cement render, blocked air bricks, raised garden levels or modern paints, or simply by drying washing indoors with the windows shut.

ul: Condensation: by far the most common. Warm moist air from cooking, showers and drying clothes settles on cold walls and windows, and black mould grows. It is fixed with ventilation and heating, not damp proofing. See condensation and ventilation in Leeds.
Penetrating damp: water getting in from outside, through a leaking gutter, failed pointing or a cracked render. Fix the leak first.
Rising damp: ground water drawn up through walls with no working damp proof course. It is less common than many people think. See rising damp treatment in Leeds.

p: A good damp survey identifies the cause before anyone sells you a treatment. Some damp companies offer free surveys and then quote for injection damp proofing whatever the problem. An independent survey costs money but tells you the truth. MyBuilder's 2026 guide puts damp surveys at about £150 to £500. See damp surveys in Leeds and our damp survey cost guide.

guide.h2: Damp and mould in rented homes
p: If you rent and have damp or mould, report it to your landlord in writing. Landlords must deal with serious damp and mould hazards, and the government has published guidance for landlords on the health risks of damp and mould. If your landlord does not act, Leeds City Council's private sector housing team can inspect.

guide.h2: Questions to ask a damp specialist
ul: What type of damp is this, and what caused it?
What evidence have you used besides a moisture meter?
Is the guarantee insurance backed, and what does it cover?
Will you need to remove plaster, and who replasters?
Could better ventilation solve this instead?

faqs.q: How do I know if I have rising damp or condensation?
faqs.a: Condensation usually shows as black mould in corners, on window reveals and behind furniture, worse in winter. Rising damp shows as a tide mark up to about a metre above the floor, often with salts on the plaster. A survey will confirm which.
Only if the survey finds a damp proofing problem. Many damp issues are condensation or leaks, which need ventilation or repairs instead of chemical injection.

faqs.q: How much does a damp survey cost?
faqs.a: MyBuilder's 2026 guide puts most damp surveys at £150 to £500 depending on the property and the tools used, such as thermal imaging.
Damp and mould can affect health, especially for people with asthma, allergies or weak immune systems, children and older people. Deal with the cause promptly.
